elements.text: WHAT YOU SHIP, AND WHERE IT RUNS
A harness competition, not a prompt-writing exercise
You ship an agent runtime that solves tasks, and you are scored on capability, cost and time simultaneously.
Your src/ is mounted here. Its only egress is a proxy to the course API at api.cs2680.com.
The repository lives at /app. A small HTTP server (src/sandbox_server.py) exposes /health, /exec, /read, /write on port 8000. Task containers have no network at all.
tasks on the leaderboard, numbered 1 to 26 - you choose how many to grade
The task environment has 26 tasks in 3 types of containers, with the agent and the task in separate containers accessed over HTTP requests. Evaluation is offline and sandboxed.

The count of 3 is the briefing slide's. The Assignment 3 spec page heads the same section "Two kinds of containers" and its own diagram shows the agent container, the task container and a grading container.
The dispatcher passes the task info to your agent
Your agent works on the task and generates a patch
The result is sent back to the agent
src/ holds the agent logic and the sandbox requests. Zipped, it is the ONLY file uploaded to the leaderboard: src.zip.
dispatcher and evaluation_scripts are the same code used on the leaderboard. Do not modify them for local testing.
next_task . extract_patch(k) / submit_patch(k, text) . evaluate(k) -> {"tests_failed": F, "tests_total": T, "attempt": a} . continue_task(k) . done(k, reason, iterations) . logger(k)
At most 5 tasks run in parallel. init.sh and package_claude_sessions.py generate the session logs, which carry no points of their own.

slides.title: Budgets, tiers, and the submission queue

elements.text: THE LIMITS ARE ENFORCED BY THE RUNTIME
Budgets, tiers, and the submission queue
Prices per 1M tokens. You may use any of the three, as many of them as you like, in one run.

Leaderboard: log in with the Canvas email and the password "Cs2680-<your 8-digit student ID>". Submit src.zip. Only one submission is queued at a time, so cancel a submission that does not look promising - a cancelled submission still counts and consumes the daily budget.
The budget is part of the task definition, not a courtesy: the first time you must trade success against cost.
the number of tasks your run solved
what the course API account was charged, divided by tasks solved
end-to-end host clock, from the first task opened to the last task done

Ranked in skyline layers over the three metrics.
At least solve 7 tasks to enter the skyline; fewer than 7 rank below all of them, ordered by tasks solved alone.
A dominates B if it is at least as good on all three metrics and better on one.
Ranks count everyone ahead of it: 1, 1, 1, 4, ...
score = max(81 - r, 50) if any submission achieves the baseline, otherwise 81 - r

The baseline solves 16 tasks in 4 hours within a limit of $10, and credit is given if any submission achieves it. Examples: rank 1 scores 80, rank 12 scores 69, rank 40 scores 50 with the baseline and 41 without.
Assignment 3 is worth 20% of the grade.
Formula as published on the Assignment 3 spec page; the course policy page states a different form, and the two published pages do not agree.
You are graded on capability, cost and time at once - the skyline, not the top score, is the objective.
The runtime contract is fixed: 26 tasks, offline-only, 5-way parallel, 35 min per evaluate(), $10 per run.
Clear the 16-task baseline, then win on efficiency; a cancelled submission still burns budget.

Out: Mon Oct 5
Due: Tue Oct 20, 11:59pm, and no late days.
Effort estimate: 10-15 hours.
Missing the deadline scores 0 for the leaderboard.
The writeup must be your own work; the video is 3 minutes, with your face and your own voice.
This is the applied form of the last three lectures: build the harness, measure it, and win on the skyline.
